1.title: Developing with AWS Lambda
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Developing with A W S Lambda. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Grant Lambda functions access to private resources in V P Cs (one point two.one). Configure functions with environment variables and parameters (one point two.two). Handle event lifecycles and errors with destinations and dead-letter queues (one point two.three). Integrate Lambda with A W S services by using code, event source mappings and destinations (one point two.four). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: The Lambda model
1.text: The Lambda model. A W S Lambda runs your code in response to events without servers to manage. You pay per request and per millisecond of compute. A function has a handler, a runtime, an execution role and configuration.

1.title: Configuration
1.text: Configuration. Memory. one hundred twenty-eight megabytes to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes; C P U grows with memory. Timeout. Up to fifteen minutes. Environment variables. Configuration without code change; encrypted at rest (use K M S or Secrets Manager for secrets). Layers. Shared libraries or dependencies attached to functions. Concurrency. Reserved (guarantee and cap) and provisioned (pre-warmed, no cold start). Versions and aliases. Immutable versions; aliases point to versions and enable traffic shifting. slash tmp. Ephemeral storage, five hundred twelve megabytes by default, up to ten gigabytes. Execution role. The I A M role the function uses to call A W S. Extensions. Add tools (monitoring, security) that run alongside the function. limits change over time.

1.title: Configuration, continued
1.text: Configuration. The figure shows this: A Lambda function inside a V P C reaching private resources.

1.title: Lambda in a VPC
1.text: Lambda in a V P C. By default a function runs outside your V P C and cannot reach private resources (for example an R D S database). To reach them, configure the function with V P C subnets and security groups. Reach a private database. Attach the function to private subnets with a security group that the database allows. Reach the internet from a V P C function. A nat gateway (or V P C endpoints for A W S services). Many connections to R D S. Use R D S Proxy to pool connections. Exam tip: A V P C-attached Lambda loses internet access unless you add a nat gateway or a V P C endpoint.

1.title: Invocation types, errors and destinations
1.text: Invocation types, errors and destinations. Synchronous. Who calls: A P I Gateway, S D K Request Response. Retries: The caller handles errors. Asynchronous. Who calls: S three, S N S, Event Bridge, S D K Event. Retries: Lambda retries twice by default, then uses destinations or a D L Q. Event source mapping (polling). Who calls: S Q S, Kinesis, Dynamo D B Streams: Lambda polls and invokes. Retries: Depends on the source; failed batches retry.

1.title: Invocation types, errors and destinations, continued
1.text: Invocation types, errors and destinations. Destinations. Send success or failure results (with details) to S Q S, S N S, Event Bridge or Lambda. Dead-letter queue. Send failed async events to S Q S or S N S. Partial batch response. For S Q S or Kinesis, report only the failed items so the rest are not retried. Bisect on error or max retry. Kinesis and Dynamo D B Streams: split a failing batch to isolate the bad record. Exam tip: For S Q S-triggered Lambda, set the queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout, and configure a D L Q on the queue (not on the function). Exam tip: Reserved concurrency guarantees and caps; provisioned concurrency removes cold starts. Do not swap them.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A Lambda function must read from a database in a private subnet. What must the developer configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Attach the function to the V P C subnets with a suitable security group. V P C configuration lets the function reach private resources.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. After attaching a function to a V P C, calls to a public A P I time out. What is the best fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Add a nat gateway for the function's subnets. V P C-attached functions need nat or endpoints to reach outside the V P C.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An asynchronous Lambda invocation keeps failing and events are lost. Which feature keeps the failed events? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A dead-letter queue or a failure destination. D L Qs and destinations capture failed asynchronous events.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which change gives a function more C P U? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Increase its memory. C P U is allocated in proportion to memory.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A function polling an S Q S queue should retry only the failed messages of a batch. What should the developer use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Partial batch response (report batch item failures). Partial batch responses return only the failed items.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How can a team remove cold start latency for a latency-sensitive function? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Provisioned concurrency. Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments initialized.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the maximum Lambda timeout? Answer: fifteen minutes. Question two. What memory range can a function use? Answer: one hundred twenty-eight megabytes to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes. Question three. How many times does Lambda retry an asynchronous invocation by default? Answer: Twice.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which event sources does Lambda poll? Answer: S Q S, Kinesis and Dynamo D B Streams (event source mappings). Question five. What is the difference between reserved and provisioned concurrency? Answer: Reserved guarantees and caps concurrency; provisioned pre-warms environments. Question six. What attaches shared libraries to many functions? Answer: Lambda layers.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Config: memory one hundred twenty-eight-ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes (C P U follows), timeout fifteen minutes, env vars, layers, aliases. V P C: subnets plus security groups; nat or endpoints for outside access; R D S Proxy. Invocation: sync, async (two retries, D L Q, destinations), polling (S Q S, Kinesis, Dynamo D B Streams). Concurrency: reserved (guarantee) versus provisioned (no cold start).
